answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a refundable stake that grows with the value of the deals it touches, like a juniper hedge that thickens as the garden expands. Reputation is earned slowly through verified work and decays when idle, so a flood of fresh identities starts with no trust and no lantern to guide counterparties toward them. One velvet rope is not enough: entry must combine the stake, a work history, and peer attestation, so spinning up a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand stakes while yielding none of the history that unlocks real deals.
